welcome.title: Welcome, Explorer!
welcome.pari_tip: There are no wrong ideas in this workbook. Try your best, ask questions, and have fun learning about AI!

syllabus.objective: I can tell machines that use AI from machines that don't.
I can name sensors that help machines see, hear and feel.
I can find a pattern and predict what comes next.
I can sort things into groups using their features.
I can write steps in the right order.
I can give clear instructions to a machine.
I can keep my private information safe.
I can use technology in a kind and balanced way.

units.title: Smart or Not?
learn_paragraphs:
Machines help us every day. A fan, a toaster and a bicycle do the same job
again and again.
Some machines can do more. They can notice things, learn from examples
and make choices. We call this Artificial Intelligence, or AI.
AI is not magic and it is not alive. People build AI and teach it.

new_words.definition: when a machine can notice, learn and decide
a list of steps to do a job
a good mix of screen time and other activities

units.did_you_know: The word “robot” was first used in a play written in 1920.
units.think_and_talk: Is a toy car that runs on batteries AI? Why or why not?
units.self_check: I can tell machines that use AI from machines that don't.

units.title: How Machines Sense
learn_paragraphs:
We use our senses to know the world: we see, hear, smell, taste and touch.
Machines use sensors. A camera helps a machine see. A microphone helps
it hear. A touch screen feels your finger.
Sensors collect information. AI uses that information to understand what is
happening.

new_words.definition: a sensor that takes pictures
a computer program that chats with you
something that helps us tell things apart

units.did_you_know: Automatic doors in malls use sensors to know when someone is coming.
units.think_and_talk: Which sense do you think is the hardest for a machine? Why?
units.self_check: I can name sensors that help machines see, hear and feel.

units.title: Patterns Everywhere
learn_paragraphs:
A pattern is something that repeats. Days of the week, stripes on a zebra
and a traffic light all have patterns.
When we find a pattern, we can predict what comes next.
AI is very good at finding patterns in lots and lots of examples.

new_words.definition: things that belong together
words that tell someone what to do
being friendly and caring

units.did_you_know: Weather apps look at patterns in past weather to guess tomorrow's weather.
units.think_and_talk: How does finding a pattern help you guess what comes next?
units.self_check: I can find a pattern and predict what comes next.

units.title: Sorting and Grouping
learn_paragraphs:
We sort things into groups by colour, shape or size.
To sort, we look at features: does it have wings? Does it live in water?
AI sorts too. It can sort photos of cats and dogs, or good emails and junk
emails.

which step comes first, next and last
a secret word that locks an account

units.did_you_know: Some post offices use machines that read addresses and sort letters automatically.
units.think_and_talk: What features help you tell a cat from a dog?
units.self_check: I can sort things into groups using their features.

units.title: Step by Step
learn_paragraphs:
An algorithm is a list of steps in the right order.
Brushing your teeth has steps. If you mix up the order, it does not work!
Computers and robots need clear steps. They do exactly what we tell them.

new_words.definition: something that repeats in the same way
to guess what comes next
only for you and your family

units.did_you_know: A recipe is an algorithm for cooking!
units.think_and_talk: What happens if a robot follows the steps in the wrong order?

units.title: Talking to Machines
learn_paragraphs:
Voice assistants and chatbots are machines we can talk to.
They understand best when our instructions are clear and short, like “Set
a timer for 5 minutes.”
Always be polite, and check important answers with a grown-up.

new_words.definition: to do or happen again
time spent using phones, TV or computers
a way we know the world, like seeing

units.did_you_know: Voice assistants turn your voice into words before they try to understand it.
units.think_and_talk: Why should we say please and thank you, even to a machine?
units.self_check: I can give clear instructions to a machine.

units.title: Safe Online
learn_paragraphs:
Some information is private: your full name, home address, phone number,
school name and passwords.
Do not share private information with strangers, games or apps unless a
grown-up says it is okay.
If something online makes you feel worried, tell a trusted adult straight
away.

new_words.definition: a machine part that collects information
a speaker you can talk to
to put things into groups

units.did_you_know: A strong password is long and mixes letters, numbers and symbols.
units.think_and_talk: What would you do if a game asked for your home address?
units.self_check: I can keep my private information safe.

units.title: Kind with Tech
learn_paragraphs:
Technology can help us learn, create and talk to family far away.
We should be kind in messages, take breaks from screens and play outside
too. This is called balance.
AI should be made to help everyone, including people who cannot see or
hear well.

new_words.definition: one small action
a grown-up who keeps you safe
a helper you talk to with your voice

units.did_you_know: Resting your eyes by looking at something far away is good during screen time.
units.think_and_talk: How can AI help people who cannot see or hear well?
